character_sheet: A hostile carnivorous plant: a 9x8x9 base on fifty-two root pieces, a stem of sixteen bulbous blocks rising to a ring of eleven zero-thickness petals and a twenty-three-plate head, four leaves of thirteen to fifteen chained segments that curl around the stem, and a fifteen-segment tongue folded like an accordion that lashes out forty-five units (TriffidModel.java:382-1276, 178 parts). 100 HP, 20 damage, 12 armour and a speed of 0.13 it never uses: it has no wander goal and re-anchors itself every hundred ticks (MobStats.java:132; EntityTriffid.java:56-71, :135-137). Closed (the synched DATA_OPEN_CLOSED at 0, :44-45) it cannot be hurt (:186-193); it opens one roll in eight every eighty ticks (:210-215) or whenever prey - anything but creepers, the ender reaper, its own kind, the two terrors, the pitch black, dragons and creative players - enters its 10-block box (:218-221, :264-277), turning to face it every tick (:138-146); within 5 blocks it raises its attacking flag and bites every 1-in-10 tick for 20 (:222-228, :42-43). A hit that lands closes it for 300 ticks, roots it and clears its fire (:150-177, :122-129, :200-204). It spawns wherever it is placed (:280-284; ModEntities.java:302-304). Read it as a trap plant: leaves curled tight when closed, swaying wide when open, the tongue whipping out straight and snapping back while it feeds.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (TriffidRenderer.java:23; shadow 0.3, :25) on a 532x715 sheet (TriffidModel.java:1276), triffid.png (TriffidRenderer.java:19); the hitbox is 2.0 x 4.0 (ModEntities.java:302-304). The original's ModelTriffid(1.0f) argument was the wingspeed (TriffidModel.java:21), not a scale. The four leaves and the tongue are position chains the code re-places each tick (:1283-1349, :1357-1395, :1593-1616) - key the joints, not the positions.

groups.name: leaves
groups.axis: z (the left and right leaves) and x (the front and back leaves), each segment placed along the one before
groups.amplitude: open: pi x 0.039 = 0.1225 rad (7 deg) per segment at 0.25 rad/tick, accumulating along the chain (up to ±1.8 rad at a 15-segment tip); closed: a fixed +0.1225 rad per segment - the cosine's peak held, the leaves curled tight around the stem; the root segments about their rests (-0.95 / +0.95 roll, -0.75 / +0.75 pitch), each next segment placed 1-6 px along the previous one's angle
groups.plain: the four leaves curl in and uncurl on one slow wave while the plant is open, the bend growing from root to tip; closed, they hold the full curl
groups.math: a = openClosed == 0 ? 0.1225 : cos(t * 0.25 * 1.0) * pi * 0.039; left: l1.zRot = -0.95 + a, then seg.zRot = prev.zRot + a with seg placed j px along prev (leafpartA); right: l31.zRot = 0.95 - a, then prev.zRot - a (leafpartC); front: l16.xRot = -0.75 - a, then prev.xRot - a (leafpartB); back: l44.xRot = 0.75 + a, then prev.xRot + a (leafpartD)
groups.source: TriffidModel.java:1283-1349 (the chains), :1593-1616 (the four leafpart helpers); wingspeed 1.0 (:21)
groups.phase: the synched DATA_OPEN_CLOSED int (EntityTriffid.java:44-45): 1 opens the wave, 0 holds the curl
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.25 x 1.0: the natural period is 25.1 ticks; closed there is no period - the angle is the constant 0.1225

groups.name: tongue
groups.axis: z, each segment placed along the one before
groups.amplitude: attacking: |cos(t x 0.25)| x pi x 0.5 - a sweep from 90 deg to 0 and back every 12.6 ticks, applied with alternating sign to the fourteen chained segments about a -0.6 offset, so the accordion unfolds to a straight 45-unit lash and folds back; not attacking: 90 deg held - the tongue fully folded; the segments are placed 6 / 3 / 3 / 3 / 3 / 3 / 6 / 6 / 6 / 6 / 6 / 6 / 3 px along the one before; all yaws 0
groups.plain: the tongue whips out straight and snaps back into its folds while the plant feeds; at rest it stays folded up at the mouth
groups.math: a = attacking ? |cos(t * 0.25 * 1.0) * pi * 0.5| : pi/2; t15.zRot = -a - 0.6; t14.zRot = a - 0.6 (placed 6 along t15); t13 = -a - 0.6 (3 along); t12 = a - 0.6; t11 = -a - 0.6; t10 = a - 0.6; t9 = -a - 0.6 (3 along); t8 = a - 0.6 (6 along); t7 ... t3 alternating (6 along each); t2 and t1 placed 3 along t3; every tN.yRot = 0
groups.phase: the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (EntityTriffid.java:42-43; 1 while prey is within 5 blocks on the 1-in-10 pass :222-228, 0 otherwise :229-234 and on a hit :165, :175) selects the lash
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.25: the cosine's period is 25.1 ticks, the absolute value halves it to 12.6 per lash

behaviour: Two synched states drive everything (EntityTriffid.java:42-45). DATA_OPEN_CLOSED (TriffidModel.java:1283): closed, every leaf segment adds a fixed 0.1225 rad to the one before, so the four leaves - 13 to 15 segments each, placed link by link (:1284-1349, :1593-1616) - hold a tight curl around the stem; open, the same angle sways as a 25-tick cosine between +0.1225 and -0.1225 per segment, and the leaves breathe from the full curl to a full uncurl, the tips swinging up to 1.8 rad.

DATA_ATTACKING (:1350-1355): at rest the fifteen tongue segments hold 90 degrees alternating about -0.6 - an accordion folded at the mouth; attacking, |cos| sweeps that angle from 90 to 0 and back every 12.6 ticks, so the chain (:1357-1395, placed 3 and 6 px per segment) shoots out into a straight 45-unit lash and folds back - the bite's motion, though the hurt itself is the 1-in-10 pass (EntityTriffid.java:222-228).

The base, roots, the sixteen stem blocks, the eleven petals and the twenty-three head plates are static; there is no head look, and the entity turns its whole body to face prey every tick (EntityTriffid.java:138-146). It does not walk: no wander goal, a re-anchor to its own position every hundred ticks (:135-137), no pushing (:117-120), and no horizontal motion during the hurt lockout (:122-129).

wishlist: in `open`: the code sways every leaf segment by one angle (TriffidModel.java:1287-1349) — let the tips lag the roots so the leaves ripple rather than hinge; the sixteen stem blocks and the petal ring are static (:382-1276), a slow stem sway would sell a living plant
in `attack`: the tongue lash the code draws (:1350-1395) is a uniform accordion — a whip that cracks at the tip on the hurt tick (EntityTriffid.java:222-228)
in `close`: a snap of the leaves and a shudder of the head plates on the hit (EntityTriffid.java:168-176); the head is static today
in `idle` (closed): a slow breath of the curl and a twitch of the folded tongue - a rooted plant needs a tell that it is alive
formulas: `TriffidModel.poseFrom` and the four leaf helpers (TriffidModel.java:1288-1417; leafpartA :1601-1605, leafpartB :1607-1611, leafpartC :1613-1617, leafpartD :1619-1623; orig ModelTriffid.java:1275-1400 in `render` (func_78088_a, :1269-1585) with leafpartA :1597-1601, leafpartC :1603-1607, leafpartB :1609-1613, leafpartD :1615-1619 (func_78087_a at :1593-1595 is a bare super call; the original's render then rotates the whole model -90 degrees about Y at :1404, which the port's renderToBuffer does not - the register's draft line), wingspeed 1.0 from `new ModelTriffid(1.0f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:459 - the port's WINGSPEED): closed, the fold is 0.122522116 per link; open, it is the cosine of the age in ticks times 0.25 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.039. Four leaf chains follow, each link rotated by its parent's angle plus the fold and placed j units from the parent along the sine and cosine of the parent's angle in the original's double arithmetic: the first chain (l1, then l2 .. l15 with leaf3 after l3; j = 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, 6, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2) rolls from -0.95 plus the fold, its root placed at -7 plus 5 times the sine of its roll, plus 3, in x and 10 minus 5 times the cosine, plus 3, in y, each link at the parent's y minus j times the cosine and x plus j times the sine of the parent's roll; the second chain (l31, then l32 .. l43 with leaf32 after l32; j = 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 1) rolls from 0.95 minus the fold, its root at 7 plus 5 times the sine, minus 3, in x and 10 minus 5 times the cosine, plus 3, in y, the links by minus the fold with the same placement; the third chain (l16, then l17 .. l30; j = 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 2, 2, 2) pitches from -0.75 minus the fold, its root at 10 plus 5 times the cosine of its pitch in y and -9 minus 5 times the sine, minus 3, in z, the links by minus the fold and placed at the parent's y plus j times the sine and z minus j times the cosine of the parent's pitch; the fourth chain (l44, then l45 .. l57 with leaf49 after l49; j = 5, 4, 3, 4, 3, 5, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2) pitches from 0.75 plus the fold, its root's pivot the bind, the links by the fold and placed at the parent's y minus j times the sine and z plus j times the cosine. Attacking, the tentacle angle is the absolute value of the cosine of the age times 0.25 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.5; not attacking, it is pi over 2. From the fifteenth link down to the third the links roll alternately by minus the angle minus 0.6 (the fifteenth) and the angle minus 0.6, each placed from the link above - 6 units for the fourteenth and for the eighth down to the third, 3 units for the thirteenth down to the ninth - at the link above's y minus that many times the sine and x minus that many times the cosine of the link above's roll (the fifteenth's pivot the bind); the first and second links are placed 3 units from the third the same way; the yaw of the third to the fifteenth links is set to 0. The walking speed, the walk position and the head angles play no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (TriffidGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
